clue.text: Innocent chap in trouble driven to remove chattels

definitions.note: the definition describes a vehicle, so it stands for a noun

indicators.note: something in trouble is in disorder, so these letters are thrown into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An innocent man in difficulties is forced to have his possessions taken away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in trouble' rearranges INNOCENT CHAP. 'driven' looks like 'forced', but the definition is a vehicle that is driven when household goods are moved.
explanation.definitionFit: A large furniture removal van, the kind driven to carry off household goods, has this old British name.

clue.text: Golf score can make a good story

parts.note: par is the standard score for a hole in golf
to be able means one can

explanation.surface: A round of golf at par makes a fine tale to tell afterwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A simple story told to teach a moral lesson, as in the Gospels, is a good story in the moral sense.

clue.text: Aunt disconcerted and embarrassed, being temperamentally disposed that way

indicators.note: being disconcerted means being thrown into confusion, so the letters of the word before are jumbled

parts.note: someone embarrassed goes red in the face

explanation.surface: An aunt is flustered and blushing, as is her temperament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disconcerted' doubles as the aunt's embarrassment in the surface, but it only signals the shuffle of the four letters before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a particular temperament, as in good-natured or ill-natured, is being disposed that way by nature.

clue.text: Unexpectedly able to speak in a flowery style

indicators.note: something happening unexpectedly is out of its usual order, so the next word's letters are rearranged

parts.note: to orate is to speak formally

explanation.surface: Someone surprisingly finds they can talk in an ornate manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unexpectedly' reads as an adverb on the speaking, but it signals a shuffle of the word beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ornate, highly detailed language is described as elaborate, rich in embellishment like flowery prose.

clue.text: Can't bear inordinate haste

definitions.note: a verb phrase in the third person, matching the verb form

indicators.note: inordinate literally means out of order, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone cannot stand excessive hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: To be unable to bear something is to loathe it, a plain synonym.

clue.text: He takes risks when another takes cover

definitions.text: He takes risks when another takes cover

parts.words: He takes risks when another takes cover
parts.note: read as a sentence about a daredevil and a coward, but it describes a company that accepts a client's risk when the client buys a policy

explanation.surface: A brave man exposes himself while his companion hides.
explanation.definitionFit: A company that underwrites a policy accepts the financial risk when the policyholder buys protection.

clue.text: Seasoning duck with a twist of orange

parts.note: a duck is a score of nought in cricket, the letter O

indicators.note: a twist of something turns it around, so the next word's letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Duck à l'orange flavoured with a sliver of peel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a twist of' sounds like a citrus garnish for duck à l'orange; here it signals a shuffle of the fruit's name.
explanation.definitionFit: This aromatic herb, wild marjoram, is a common seasoning in Italian cooking.

clue.text: Contemplating truancy?

parts.note: read literally, someone thinking about being away from school is minded to be away

explanation.definitionFit: Being forgetful or distracted is the everyday sense; the clue reads the compound as inclined to stay away.

clue.text: Capital investment for father?

parts.note: sounds like finance for dad, but capital is the head, an investment is something put on, and Father is a priest

explanation.surface: A financial stake made on behalf of one's dad.
explanation.definitionFit: A square cap worn by Roman Catholic clergy is a head covering, something a priest is invested with.

clue.text: Hardy lass has time to for a bit of artistic piecework

parts.note: Tess of the d'Urbervilles is the heroine of a Thomas Hardy novel
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A Thomas Hardy heroine finds time for some craftwork.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue as printed reads 'to for'; the 'to' is a stray link word and does nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A small tile of stone or glass set in a mosaic is one piece of an artwork assembled from bits.

clue.text: Its main trade is in disarray, requiring control

indicators.note: disarray is disorder, so the letters of the preceding words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A business whose chief commerce is chaotic needs managing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is in disarray' rearranges ITS MAIN TRADE; 'requiring' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To manage or run something is to control it, a close synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Measure lawyers try to ban

parts.note: an em is a printer's measure of width
the Bar is the body of barristers
to have a go is to try

explanation.surface: Lawyers attempt to outlaw a proposed measure.
explanation.definitionFit: An official prohibition, especially on trade with a country, is a type of ban.

clue.text: Unending massacre can result in bitter comment

indicators.note: the dropped word's letters can turn into something else, so they are rearranged
something unending has lost its end, so the last letter of the next word is dropped

explanation.surface: A slaughter that drags on may provoke scathing remarks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unending' cuts MASSACRE to MASSACR, which 'can result in' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutting irony used to mock or wound is the sense of a bitter remark.

clue.text: Mind about mid-14 drift

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece is placed around the other

parts.note: to tend is to mind or look after

indicators.note: mid- points to the central letter of the answer at 14 across

parts.note: a cross-reference to the solution at 14 across

explanation.surface: Thinking about the drifting middle of the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mid-14' picks R, the middle letter of 14 across, and 'about' wraps TEND round it.
explanation.definitionFit: A general tendency or direction of movement, as in the drift of opinion, is a trend.

clue.text: For No 10 a new PM

indicators.note: making something new remakes it, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: 10 is ten

explanation.surface: Number 10 Downing Street gets a fresh Prime Minister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No 10' looks like Downing Street and PM like the Prime Minister; 'new' rearranges FOR NO TEN A.
explanation.definitionFit: PM, post meridiem, marks the hours after noon, the later part of the day.

clue.text: A blow in an attempt to achieve parity

definitions.text: A blow in an attempt to achieve parity

parts.words: A blow in an attempt to achieve parity
parts.note: describes striking back to even the score, the idea of a returned blow for a blow received

explanation.surface: Someone hits out trying to level matters.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means retaliation in kind, giving back exactly what was received to make things equal.

clue.text: Living man

parts.note: seems to mean a man who is alive, but a living is a church benefice and this man holds one

explanation.definitionFit: The holder of a church benefice, called a living, is the parson who occupies the post.

clue.text: Take encouragement in comfort

definitions.meaning: to brighten up and feel more hopeful
to console someone and lift their spirits

explanation.surface: Someone finds reassurance in being consoled.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to become more cheerful and to make someone else feel better.

clue.text: Go off at the wrong time

definitions.text: Go off at the wrong time

parts.words: Go off at the wrong time
parts.note: sounds like leaving at a bad moment, but describes a gun or engine discharging badly

explanation.surface: Someone departs at an inconvenient moment.
explanation.definitionFit: A weapon or engine that fails to discharge properly, or fires too early, does this.

clue.text: Social worker is succeeding with opponents

indicators.note: succeeding means coming after, so the word is placed after the insect

parts.note: the ant is a social insect and a worker

explanation.surface: A social worker does well against those who oppose her work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Social worker' suggests a welfare officer; it is the colony insect, followed by IS.
explanation.definitionFit: People against something are informally called this, from the prefix meaning against.

clue.text: A notion to be cast as the Merchant of Venice

indicators.note: casting can mean throwing things about, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: An idea about who should play the title role in Shakespeare's comedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be cast' suggests theatre casting but rearranges A NOTION.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare's play the title character, the merchant who borrows from Shylock, bears this name.

clue.text: They may commemorate different battles

indicators.note: different letters are made by changing their order, so the next word is rearranged

explanation.surface: Memorials may be raised to various battles.
explanation.definitionFit: Inscribed stone or metal plaques are often put up to commemorate people or events.

clue.text: Gets ready to eat, or to be eaten

definitions.text: Gets ready to eat, or to be eaten

parts.words: Gets ready to eat, or to be eaten
parts.note: one reading is changing for dinner, the other is preparing a salad or a bird for the table

explanation.surface: Someone prepares for a meal, or perhaps to become one.
explanation.definitionFit: One changes into formal clothes for dinner, and a cook prepares a fowl or salad for serving.

clue.text: Explosive device found on the beach

definitions.meaning: an artillery projectile filled with explosive
the hard casing of a sea creature washed up on the sand

explanation.surface: A bomb is discovered on the seashore.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both an artillery projectile and the hard outer case of a mollusc.

clue.text: O to be in credit for a month!

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit

explanation.surface: An exclamation of longing to be in the black for a while.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface echoes Browning's 'Oh, to be in England'.
explanation.definitionFit: The tenth month of the calendar year is a month.

clue.text: Rodents carry out an unusual crime

parts.note: to do something is to carry it out

indicators.note: something unusual is out of the ordinary, so the next word's letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Rodents commit an odd offence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'an unusual crime' reads as an odd offence; 'unusual' signals a shuffle of the offence word.
explanation.definitionFit: These small hibernating mammals, related to squirrels, are rodents.

clue.text: An outside line to ring

parts.note: sounds like a telephone line to call out on, but describes a straight line touching a circle from outside

explanation.surface: Someone wants a phone line to call out.
explanation.definitionFit: In geometry, a straight line touching a circle at one point lies outside it.

clue.text: Names said to be used for mountains

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the word for the range is to be heard rather than read

parts.note: the Appalachians are a mountain range in eastern North America

explanation.surface: Titles reportedly given to mountain ranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Formal titles or designations, as in a wine's appellation, are names.
